finding: Passed review on 2026-11-20 at low confidence after the two bulletins carrying the labor ends were re-read and matched (Hyundai 0.5 M/H, FCA 0.9 Hrs). There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so there is nothing to call too wide or too narrow; this is a first build. What can be built (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2012 Toyota Corolla about $206-$740 (parts $146.26-$595.67, 0.5-0.9 hour); midsize 2015 Subaru Forester 2.5i about $309-$583 (parts $236.95-$439.45, 0.6-0.9 hour); truck 2015 Ram 1500 5.7L about $268-$1,152 (parts $160.21-$832, 0.9-2 hours); luxury 2012 Lexus ES 350 about $319-$821 for one of its two rear mufflers (parts $259.43-$676.97, 0.5-0.9 hour). The part is most of every total: the labor is roughly $60 to $320. Two caveats on the lows added in the fourth attempt. The truck low ($160.21) is a stock-style Walker muffler on a page that says brand-new, calls it direct fit and bolt-on and lists the 2015 Ram 1500, but other sellers list the same part for the single-exhaust truck only and one describes it as a muffler without pipes, so on some trucks fitting it means cutting the old muffler from its tail pipe and clamping the new one, which takes longer than a bolted swap. For trucks with the factory dual exhaust no stock-style direct-fit muffler was found; the direct-fit parts seen are performance mufflers at about $426-$508, which would put that truck's low near $534-$616. The luxury low ($259.43) is a direct-fit kit on a page that says new and names the 2007-2012 ES 350 in its title; the page does not say which of the car's two mufflers it replaces, though the genuine number it names is in the same series as the left-hand genuine part used for the high, and the kit for the other muffler costs the same ($259.44). Nothing in the parts or hours is null now. Cheaper Walker direct-fit mufflers for the ES 350 were seen at roughly $129-$211, but each page failed one test: it printed no model years, did not say the part was new, or showed no price. How solid the labor times are: two examples have a time for the example vehicle, and neither is a maker document. The Forester's 0.6 hour is a Subaru book time quoted by a named mechanic, and the Ram's 2 hours is a parts seller's figure written for an owner fitting a bolt-on muffler at home (two listings for the truck say 2 hours and one says 1 hour). Every other range end is a maker-stated time for a different vehicle: Hyundai's 0.5 hour for the centre muffler on the 2014-2015 Tucson and FCA's 0.9 hour for the muffler on the 2015 Ram 2500 and 3500 pickups. No maker-stated time with a unit was found for the Corolla, Forester, Ram 1500 or ES 350. Four maker figures support the range without being used as ends because each includes an inspection or prints no unit: Mazda 0.4 hour (2019 CX-5 Turbo), FCA 0.3 hour (2020 Jeep Cherokee, inspect and replace), Kia 0.4 hour (2023 Sportage centre muffler, inspect and replace) and Subaru 0.2 with no unit (2015-2017 Legacy and Outback). These suggest warranty times are often shorter than 0.5 hour, so the labor range here is not low. All of them are times for bolted joints that come apart; a rusted flange or seized bolts on an older car add time, and the 0.9 hour top does not allow for that. On some vehicles the larger main muffler is part of a centre pipe that costs far more from the maker and is outside this unit; a quote for 'a muffler' on such a vehicle may be for that part. Benchmarks, from three publishers with a full installed price: RepairPal's national average is $1,138-$1,190 with parts at about $1,035, far above the built totals, while its Corolla figure ($625-$661) sits inside the built economy range and its Silverado and F-150 figures ($706-$830) sit inside the built truck range. The national figure appears to price a dearer genuine part or a larger exhaust section; the page does not say which, so that is a reading, not a finding. CostHelper gives $75-$750 or more (its readers report $80-$647, average $280, in reports dated 2010 to 2020) and Synchrony's article gives $175-$450 or more, with a maker's original muffler at up to $1,000. Both are lower than RepairPal and overlap the built economy and midsize ranges; their low ends are for cheaper universal or welded-in mufflers than the direct-fit parts priced here. A fourth entry is parts only. Confidence is low because half the labor range ends are not for the example vehicle, no example has a maker-stated time, and the truck low may need a cut and clamps on some trucks. This is an estimate, not a quote and not a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds new gaskets, clamps, bolts and rubber hangers, and labor to cut or heat rusted fasteners. Many shops recommend replacing the connecting pipe or resonator at the same time, and on cars with two rear mufflers the second one. If no bolt-on part is used, a muffler shop may cut the old one out and weld in a universal muffler, which is priced differently from this estimate. Also possible: a diagnosis or exhaust leak check fee, shop supplies and sales tax. A muffler replaced under a recall, service campaign or warranty extension is done by the dealer at no charge, so check for open campaigns first.
